summary: Reviewed gui/public/css/styles.css (sole modified file). All six ACs satisfied and code quality is high. Applied one Fix-Forward: replaced hardcoded `color: #fff` in .nav-badge with `color: var(--color-btn-text)` to align with the project-wide convention of using CSS custom properties exclusively — the same token used by .btn-primary and .btn-danger. One documentation-forward item filed for the AC/view class-name divergence. No blocking issues found; PASS.

comments.note: gui/public/css/styles.css line 750: replaced `color: #fff` with `color: var(--color-btn-text)` in .nav-badge. The project convention mandates CSS custom properties for all color values; --color-btn-text is the established token for white-on-colored-background text and is already used identically by .btn-primary and .btn-danger. The change is purely cosmetic — identical rendered output in both themes.

[documentation-forward] The error-log view emits class names `error-log-detail-row` and `error-log-detail-pre`, while the WP-012 spec AC4 names `.error-detail-row` and `.error-detail-content`. Both sets are styled via comma-selectors and rendering is correct, but a future cleanup should either (a) update the view to use the spec-aligned names, or (b) update the spec/AC4 to reflect the view's actual names, and drop the now-redundant alias selectors from styles.css.

gui/public/js/views/error-log.js: The `buildFilterBar` function rebuilds and replaces the entire filter bar DOM node on each `rebuildFilterBar()` call. For v1 this is fine, but if the filter bar ever gains more controls (e.g., a date-range picker), a fine-grained update strategy (mutate select values directly rather than replace the DOM subtree) would be less disruptive to focus management.

Overall code quality is high. XSS safety (textContent-only DOM construction), accessibility attributes (role=button, tabindex, aria-expanded), relative-time fallback handling, and dark-mode custom property cascade are all implemented correctly. The dual comma-selector aliasing for the detail panel is a pragmatic forward-compat decision — adequately documented in comments.
